---
title: "Install and launch"
---

ToFScope supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Windows portable launcher {#windows-portable}

The portable Windows release includes Python and the application dependencies.
You do not need to install Python, `uv`, or Node.js, and extraction does not require
administrator privileges. You need a browser, a folder containing supported
*TOFWERK* *TOFexplorer* HDF5 (`.h5`) acquisitions, and enough writable space for saved copies.

1. Open the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/releases)
   and expand **Assets** for a release that includes a Windows bundle.
2. Download `ToFScope-<version>-windows-x64.zip` and its `.zip.sha256` checksum.
   Older releases may not have a Windows bundle. Assets appear after the release build finishes.
3. Extract the entire ZIP into a folder owned by your Windows account.
   Keep `ToFScope.exe`, `ToFScope-cli.exe`, and `_internal` together.
   Open the extracted folder before launching; do not run the executable from inside the ZIP.
4. Double-click **ToFScope.exe**, then use **Browse…** to choose your acquisition folder.
5. Click **Start**. ToFScope opens in your default browser once the local service is ready.

Keep the launcher open while you work. **Open in browser** reopens the running app.
Save your analysis before clicking **Stop** or closing the launcher; closing a browser
tab alone does not stop the service. To change acquisition folders, stop the service,
choose another folder, and start again.

The launcher remembers the acquisition folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ToFScope`.
That directory also contains `service.log` and `launcher.log`; **Open log** opens the
service log, which is replaced each time you start. Saved analyses are separate from
these preferences and logs. Choose a writable acquisition folder if you plan to save
copies there. To configure a separate output folder, use the command-line interface
below with `ToFScope-cli.exe` in place of `tofscope`.

The x64 bundle targets Windows 10 and 11. It has also been manually exercised on
Windows 11 ARM using Windows' x64 emulation; that is not a native ARM build.

### Windows security prompts

::: {.callout-warning}
## Microsoft Defender SmartScreen

The Windows executables are currently unsigned. Windows may show **Windows protected
your PC**, **unrecognized app**, or an **unknown publisher** warning when launching a
downloaded executable. SmartScreen uses an application's reputation to help assess it;
a warning does not establish that the download is safe or unsafe.

Download from the project's [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/releases)
and verify the ZIP against the checksum attached to the same release. In PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\ToFScope-<version>-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256
```

Compare the returned hash with the value in the `.zip.sha256` file. If you trust the
download and Windows provides the option, select **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
An organization policy or Windows 11 Smart App Control may prevent this option;
contact your administrator if the application is blocked. Keep Windows security
protections enabled.

See Microsoft's guidance on [SmartScreen reputation warnings](https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/office/protect-my-pc-from-viruses)
and [Smart App Control](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-malware-protection/smart-app-control-frequently-asked-questions).
:::

### Offline use, updates, and removal

Download the ZIP on a connected machine, transfer it to the offline machine, and
extract it there. The launcher and bundled application do not need an internet
connection; your browser connects to the service on the same machine. Acquisitions
on network shares still require access to those shares.

To update, save your work and stop ToFScope. Extract the new release into a separate
folder and run its launcher. The remembered acquisition folder stays in your Windows
profile. Keep acquisition files and saved analyses outside the extracted application
folder. To remove a portable release, stop it and delete its application folder.
Removing `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ToFScope` separately clears launcher preferences and logs.

## Python installation (Windows, macOS, and Linux)

For command-line use, install Python 3.11 through 3.14 and
[*uv*](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
You can also use `pip` directly. You need an acquisition folder and enough writable
space for saved copies.

After installing `uv` using the instructions for your operating system at the link above, you can open a new terminal window and check that it is available:

```sh
uv --version
```

The following command installs ToFScope from PyPI:

```sh
uv tool install tofscope
```

If your shell cannot find `tofscope`, you can run `uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal window.

## Folder selection and launch

By default, ToFScope will only have access to whatever files are in the folder that you launch it from
(or any subfolders). You can use the `--data-root` argument to allow read-only access to another folder
(such as a network mount containing your instruments' data) and the `--output-root` argument to allow
for saving analysis results to a separate folder.

The example paths in this command should be replaced with your acquisition and saved-copy folders;
paths containing spaces need quotation marks:

```sh
tofscope --data-root "/path/to/acquisitions" --output-root "/path/to/saved-analyses"
```

On Windows, for example, use paths appropriate to your system in PowerShell:

```powershell
tofscope --data-root "C:\Data\Acquisitions" --output-root "C:\Data\Saved Analyses"
```

On Windows, the runtime directory inherits permissions from its parent. Keep it within a directory
restricted to your Windows account.

The local service will start in your terminal and the app should open automatically in your browser.
The terminal process needs to remain open while you work. After saving your analysis, you can stop the
service by returning to the terminal and pressing **Ctrl-C**.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Saving before stopping the service

Heads up! Open analyses and in-progress jobs are held in memory until you explicitly save them.
Use the **Save as** feature to save your analysis before stopping the ToFScope process, or you will
lose your data!
:::

Original acquisitions opened by ToFScope are never edited directly; the application will only save copies
to protect the original integrity of the collected data.

## Updates and removal

Using *uv*, the app can be updated with the following command:

```sh
uv tool upgrade tofscope
```

The command `uv tool uninstall tofscope` uninstalls the app. This does not delete your acquisition or saved-analysis folders.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| **`uv: command not found`** | A new terminal window and the PATH instructions printed by the uv installer may resolve the problem. |
| **`tofscope: command not found`** | You can run `uv tool update-shell`, open a new terminal window, and try again. `uv tool list` shows installed tools. |
| **No files in the picker** | `--data-root` must point to the folder containing the `.h5` files, and the service needs permission to read it. If `--data-root` is not given, ToFScope can only see files within the folder from which it was run. |
| **Browser did not open** | The terminal may contain an error message. If the service is running, `tofscope open` in another terminal window opens the existing local service. |
| **Cannot save** | The output folder must exist, be writable, and have enough free space for a full copy. Calculations must be finished or canceled and drafts finished or discarded before saving. ToFScope also will not overwrite a file, currently, so check if there is a duplicate file name in the selected folder. |
| **Port already in use** | The previous ToFScope process may need to be stopped before trying again. |

For help with startup problems, `tofscope doctor` loads the configuration and verifies the packaged frontend assets. It reports an error if either check fails; it does not diagnose every startup problem:

```sh
tofscope doctor --data-root "/path/to/acquisitions" --output-root "/path/to/saved-analyses"
```
